note: What each benchmark board measures, for the benchmark page (ticket 25) and model inspection (ticket 12). `measures`, `tasks` and `score` are quoted from the page named in `url`, fetched on `fetched`; a quote may be cut at a sentence boundary but is never reworded. `scale` says what the number on the plot is, read from the row's own field. `cost` is the basis in sources.json. `direction` is curated and is never inferred for a board with no entry. `speaks_to` is curated relevance of the quoted description to coding work, knowledge work and API-workflow evidence; it is not the source's claim, and it does not name a routing Domain or a Class that does not exist. A board with no entry is shown with no description and says so.

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.measures: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index combines a comprehensive suite of evaluation datasets to assess language model capabilities across reasoning, knowledge, maths and programming.
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.tasks: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 incorporates 10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase, GDPval-AA v2, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench v4.0, SciCode, AA-LCR v1.1, AA-Omniscience, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt.
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.score: Intelligence Index is calculated as a weighted average across four categories: Agents (30%), Coding (20%), Scientific Reasoning (20%) and General (30%).
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.cost: per task: the cost of running the Intelligence Index
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.speaks_to: composite across reasoning, knowledge, maths and programming; shown and never counted by the carry rule. Quoted category weights sit beside the source caution that the weighting is unpublished. Neither is a coding, knowledge or API-workflow score

AutomationBench.measures: It tests whether models can complete realistic SaaS workflows that span multiple simulated business apps, using REST APIs as the tool interface.
AutomationBench.tasks: We evaluate a private 657-task held-out split from AutomationBench dataset version 1.0.6. The tasks cover six business domains: Finance, HR, Marketing, Operations, Sales, and Support.
AutomationBench.score: For the headline score, a task receives 0 if the model violates any guardrail. If no guardrails are violated, the task receives the percentage of objectives the model completed. Errored tasks also score 0.
AutomationBench.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
AutomationBench.speaks_to: API-workflow relevance: REST-tool SaaS workflows, not GUI computer use. Adjacent to mechanical and impl only as multi-step tool calls against a spec; not a routing Domain or Class

AA-LCR.measures: Evaluate long context performance through testing reasoning capabilities across multiple long documents (~100k tokens measured using cl100k_base tokenizer)
AA-LCR.tasks: 100 hard text-based questions spanning 7 categories of documents (Company Reports, Industry Reports, Government Consultations, Academia, Legal, Marketing Materials, and Survey Reports)
AA-LCR.score: Model responses are evaluated using GPT-5.6 Luna (medium) as an equality checker with pass@1 scoring
AA-LCR.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
AA-LCR.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
AA-LCR.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: long-document reasoning. Coding work: scout and review at most

Omniscience.measures: AA-Omniscience is a knowledge and hallucination benchmark that measures factual reliability, rewards precise knowledge, and penalizes incorrect guesses or hallucinations.
Omniscience.tasks: The benchmark consists of 6,000 questions covering 42 topics, including Business, Humanities and Social Sciences, Health, Law, Software Engineering, and Science, Engineering and Mathematics.
Omniscience.score: Models are scored using the AA-Omniscience Index, which assigns points for correct answers, subtracts points for hallucinated responses, and keeps abstentions neutral, rewarding abstentions over incorrect guesses
Omniscience.scale: AA-Omniscience Index, below zero when wrong answers outnumber right ones
Omniscience.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
Omniscience.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: factual reliability and hallucination (42 topics; not a finance, investing or supply-chain split). Coding work: scout and review at most — a wrong fact stated with confidence is the failure it counts

GDPval.measures: GDPval-AA v2 is Artificial Analysis' evaluation framework for OpenAI's GDPval dataset. It assesses language models' capabilities on economically valuable tasks, covering 44 occupations across key sectors contributing to GDP in the United States.
GDPval.tasks: Task Submission – Models are given a task and required to produce one or more files.
GDPval.score: Pairwise Grading – A judge sampled from a panel of three frontier LLM judges blindly ranks two submissions for the same task, each created by a different model. The Elo scale is anchored to human expert deliverables at 1000.
GDPval.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
GDPval.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: professional deliverables pairwise-graded. Coding work: adjacent to impl as finished files judged against each other, not tests

Terminal-Bench 2.1.measures: A verified refresh of Terminal-Bench, developed by Stanford University researchers, the Laude Institute, and the open source community. Keeps the same 89 curated tasks across software engineering, system administration, data processing, model training, and security
Terminal-Bench 2.1.tasks: We evaluate the full Terminal-Bench v2.1 dataset (89 tasks) using the Terminus 2 agent harness in an E2B sandbox environment, with pass@1 scoring averaged over 3 repeats per task
Terminal-Bench 2.1.score: Each task ships with a verification suite that the agent must satisfy by interacting with the terminal — tasks are considered successful only if every test passes
Terminal-Bench 2.1.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
Terminal-Bench 2.1.speaks_to: Coding relevance: agentic shell work graded by tests; the task set also spans operations and science, so it is not a pure coding axis. Coding work: impl and hard-impl

GPQA Diamond.tasks: 198 questions covering biology, physics and chemistry - we test the GPQA Diamond subset of the full GPQA dataset (448 questions total), which was defined by the original authors as the highest quality subset, where both experts answer correctly and the majority of non-experts answer incorrectly
GPQA Diamond.score: 4 option multiple choice format. Regex-based answer extraction with pass@1 scoring
GPQA Diamond.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
GPQA Diamond.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
GPQA Diamond.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: scientific multiple-choice with no tools and no code. Coding work: review at most

MMMU-Pro.measures: An enhanced MMMU benchmark that eliminates shortcuts and guessing strategies to more rigorously test multimodal models across 30 academic disciplines
MMMU-Pro.score: Multiple Choice (10 options). Regex extraction, pass@1
MMMU-Pro.scale: share of questions answered correctly, 0 to 1
MMMU-Pro.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
MMMU-Pro.speaks_to: Knowledge relevance: multimodal understanding of images and text. It does not directly measure coding or API-workflow performance.

IFBench.measures: A benchmark that evaluates a model's ability to follow precise instructions in a single turn. It tests a wide range of skills, including counting, formatting, and sentence manipulation.
IFBench.tasks: Uses the single-turn IFBench dataset, which contains 294 questions
IFBench.score: Our score represents the prompt level accuracy (average across all questions and repeats)
IFBench.cost: per task: the Intelligence Index's cost, the same on every AA board
IFBench.speaks_to: Coding relevance: following precise instructions in a single turn. Coding work: mechanical — doing exactly what the brief says

Terminal-Bench 4.0.measures: Terminal-Bench is a benchmark for measuring agents' abilities to complete tasks using a terminal.
Terminal-Bench 4.0.score: Resolution rate of Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks. The whiskers span the 95% confidence interval.
Terminal-Bench 4.0.cost: whole run, not per task; the leaderboard does not say so, and sources.json records it
Terminal-Bench 4.0.speaks_to: Coding relevance: an agent and a model scored as a pair ("To test an agent and model, pass --agent and --model"); the task set is not a pure coding axis. Coding work: impl and hard-impl

SWE Refactor Bench.measures: Can a coding agent move a whole repository to a new stack — another language, framework, platform or build system — and change nothing about what it does?
SWE Refactor Bench.score: S(τ) = 1[migration happened] · 1[every check passes] · (0.4 + 0.6 · s/6) ∈ {0} ∪ [0.4, 1]. Behavioural Tests: 130,118 checks recorded from the original. All of them, or the run scores zero.
SWE Refactor Bench.speaks_to: Coding relevance: whole-repository migrations. Coding work: hard-impl — hours-long work on a whole repository
